summary: Today’s expanded edition offers 49 detailed guides, including 20 completed from earlier screened entries, and 31 additional newly screened tools. It adds 60 distinct tools to the cumulative library. Coverage spans 75 fields, 623 configured repository queries and 18 model tasks; archived search failures, partial results and bounded pages remain disclosed below. Live primary-source research supplements every field, including neural audio patching and learned light shaping. All platforms were searched equally; individual tools retain their documented platform limits. The two new GitLab guides distinguish software grants from model/service costs. None of these applications was installed or run by AI Media Scout, and no new entry earned Recommended or Ready to try without independent evidence. First profile means new to this library, not necessarily launched today. All repository queries returned successful attempts, with 122 bounded searches. One text-to-image model-task response exceeded the collector’s 2 MB archival limit; web research supplements that explicit gap. Codeberg and SourceHut access gaps are recorded separately.

Local neural music studios and synthesis were researched. OpenSuno’s primary site distinguishes MIT application code from non-commercial YuE2 and associated weights; Windows support remains experimental.
Parametric modeling and AI-agent CAD were researched through SolidCraft and SOMA. Editable geometry/export capability is distinct from verified dimensional accuracy or fabrication readiness.

The expanded search found a learned Max for Live performance mixer and an agent-driven OSC/MIDI integration. Both are screened leads with specific setup/documentation discrepancies, rather than qualified performance recommendations. RAVE and nn_tilde remain excluded because their reviewed software grants are non-commercial. The primary RAVE paper was revisited for learned audio synthesis. IRCAM’s project page returned mainly navigation in the text view; neither that partial view nor the paper changes the reviewed non-commercial software grant.

Learned caustic-image generation and neural shape-from-caustics research were examined as light-art adjacencies. The web research did not establish a newly eligible, licensed creator application. Classical caustic optimization alone is not evidence of a neural tool.
Browser AI and creative-canvas sources were researched. WebLLM provides an in-browser model runtime, whereas ordinary WebGPU effects are not automatically AI tools.

Meta’s primary IWSDK announcement describes agent-written and tested immersive-web scenes. This establishes an AI-assisted authoring route, not universal headset support or independently verified experience quality.
Creative-coding environments and neural/agent authoring were researched. Fragment’s ordinary shader and MIDI tools are not counted as AI simply because an agent could write code for them.
Primary installation software documentation includes ONNX pose detection controlling media and lights. Interaction support remains distinct from reliable unattended operation.
SOMA’s primary documentation covers AI-authored editable CadQuery models and physical-design examples. A STEP/STL export is not a guarantee of printability, load capacity or manufactured accuracy.
ForgeAX and Evoke broadened the game search from agent-authored editable code to learned interactive worlds. Their architecture and author demos do not establish universal game-production readiness.
Movens-Zero’s primary project documents recovered and generated motion from several modalities. Research/model availability alone does not establish an artist-ready animation application.
AVTR-1’s primary model card links the inference code and specifies CUDA/TensorRT and Ampere-or-newer GPU prerequisites. Weight availability and an avatar demo do not settle all software/asset terms.
Light-aware compositing and BlenderFusion research supplemented keying/compositing discovery. A paper or conventional compositor alone is not a newly reviewed open-source AI application.
Neural acoustic-field research was examined for immersive spatial sound. Conventional room simulation is not classified as neural inference without concrete evidence.

Primary volumetric-capture research describes RGB/RGB-D reconstruction into point clouds and Gaussian splats. Capture quality, synchronization and usable source licensing require separate workflow checks.

Subtitle Edit’s current primary documentation lists local/cloud speech models and AI review alongside manual subtitle tools. Recognition, translation, timing and provider privacy remain separate checks.
SVGRender and StarVector primary sources cover learned raster-to-vector and text/image-to-SVG workflows. Editable output is not proof of geometric cleanliness or design quality.
VecGlypher research generates editable vector glyphs with image/text conditioning. Source availability, font rights, script coverage and operator setup were not established merely from the paper.

Primary storyboard/comic project sites were researched. Dramai’s own page says its v0.1 ships storyboard generation while later pipeline stages remain planned, so marketing-stage diagrams are not treated as completed functionality.

OpenSlides and Amaroad primary sites describe agent-editable decks, live previews and export routes. AI provider terms and the fidelity of static PowerPoint export remain distinct from the app’s software license.
Primary research on learned restoration of historical Autochrome defects was checked. Restored appearance is not evidence that inferred historical detail is authentic.
Primary AI/scientific-visualization research and editable map workflows were researched. The survey is context rather than a newly qualified installable tool.
MIT’s Illuminate project documents learned body tracking in an interactive artwork. Artwork/media licensing alone is not a reviewed software grant or a redistributable installation package.

Ossia’s primary projection-mapping documentation includes neural pose inputs and multichannel show workflows. A documented exhibition example does not guarantee performance on another installation’s hardware.

OpenTryOn, Oxygen-TryOn and FabricTryOn primary pages were researched. Oxygen’s card explicitly uses non-commercial weights; visual garment-transfer examples do not establish a fully licensed, production-ready application.
W3C’s primary media-description guidance and local subtitle workflows were researched. AI transcription is not the same as audio description, reliable translation or verified accessible media.

Mobile and browser creative routes were searched, alongside the Android Akshar Studio documentation. OpenSlides documents small-screen editing, but browser access does not establish local model support on every phone.

KinoDraw and Paper2Video primary project pages describe narrated educational video workflows. Author examples and marketing claims remain separate from independent validation and full dependency licensing.

Learned historical-image restoration and PyPottery’s archaeological drawing tools were researched. Reconstructed detail is inferred, and an archaeological documentation tool is not automatically reliable for every conservation task.

Research extended to agentic dance, neural acoustics and olfactory media rather than staying within established categories. Paper-only evidence and promised code releases remain research leads, not qualified application entries.

TouchTwin and VibraForge primary research was examined. Vibrotactile hardware authoring alone is not an AI workflow; a newly eligible, fully licensed haptic application was not established by this pass.

NeRAF, MiNAF and Audible World Models primary pages were researched. The latter still labels code coming soon; synthesized room acoustics and controlled spectral experiments do not imply a complete real-time spatial-audio product.

OpenSlides’ primary documentation and newly examined agent/media workspaces cover editable AI-assisted production. Mock images, agent scripts and conventional rendering are distinguished from actually generated creative output.
LyriFont’s primary project describes neural music-genre analysis driving typography. Its installation concept and source link do not alone establish a reviewed, redistributable package.

MAESTRO’s primary project describes structure-aware agent planning, motion reuse and windowed editing. A convincing author example does not establish independent use or clean licensing of all motion sources.

Ink Blossom and p5.embroider primary sources were researched. The former produces AI embroidery imagery but does not establish executable machine stitch files; the latter’s ordinary procedural patterns are not inherently AI.

TMD, Tenuto and ABC-score workflows were examined. Agent-friendly text notation can support co-composition, but a deterministic engraving engine alone is not a neural composer. Tenuto’s browser and engraving extensions remain on its roadmap.
AEGIR and physically controllable relighting primary research was checked. AEGIR’s current project page says code coming soon, so its editable-light demos are not a new licensed software listing.

AromaGen and Paint by Odor primary papers broadened the search to scent interfaces and cross-sensory visualization. Hardware safety, chemical supply and software grants were not settled by these papers.

Primary inverse-rendering and text-to-CAD sites were researched. AgenticCAD explicitly uses a non-commercial software grant and therefore is not an eligible new open-source application under this policy.

Neural view/lighting representations and area-emitter inverse rendering were researched. No separately qualified new light-field authoring application was established in this pass; representation research is kept distinct from a creator-ready editor.

Neural Puppet and language-articulated-object research were checked for controllable characters. Layered character representation, articulated geometry and a reusable puppeteering application require separate evidence.

PyPottery’s current primary documentation describes SAM-assisted vessel tracing and diffusion-based ink drawing. This is useful ceramic documentation evidence, not proof of safe automated clay fabrication. Existing entries were not recycled unchanged.

AgenticCAD, CadQuery and LAM primary sources were examined. A conventional CAD kernel is not an AI tool by itself, and AgenticCAD’s non-commercial source terms exclude it from new open-source listings.

MapStory’s primary paper covers LLM scene breakdown and researched geospatial grounding. Editable animation does not guarantee correct coordinates or factual mapping; the QGIS workflow queue was also revisited.

FORM and robotic pottery research were checked. Learned material handling and shaping can inform art workflows, but the cited work does not establish a general autonomous sculpture system or a ready hardware package.
OpenToonz’s primary site and layered cartoon-character research were examined. Traditional animation software is eligible only for a concrete AI/ML feature, not merely its open-source status.

FOL·AI’s primary project describes video-conditioned synchronized sound effects and a game-walking dataset. Its page still advertises code available soon; this pass did not establish a new fully licensed installable application.
Current primary codec research includes TQCodec and token-completion bandwidth extension. Audio fidelity, codec compatibility and tool packaging remain separate from model compression claims.
Sonify’s Parallax primary artwork description combines neural art and data sonification. The accompanying TwoTone sonifier is not counted as AI merely because it appears in that ecosystem.

Primary brain-sonification research and Brain Viewer installation documentation were researched. Biosignal mapping and an AI-assisted installation are distinguished from a documented standalone creative inference tool.

VideoNeuMat, NeuMatEx and texture-space diffusion primary sources were examined. Neural material assets differ from conventional PBR maps; code coming soon or a paper-only page is not a reviewed application release.

Primary neural-camera research and camera-conditioned scene generation were checked. Lens/color matching is distinct from virtual camera reshooting, and no new qualified camera application was established merely from these papers.

COrigami research and Princeton’s primary kirigami report broadened the search. Ordinary folding simulation, AI spatial-reasoning tests and fabricated results are not interchangeable; machine-ready designs still need physical validation.

OpenCADIrrigation’s primary site describes an AI-assisted editable planning workflow, while many other results were closed hosted visualizers. A new fully reviewed source/license profile was not completed from the website alone.
Visual Anagrams’ primary paper was checked for multi-view diffusion illusions, including mosaic-like examples. A generated tiled-looking image is not automatically a physical mosaic fabrication plan.
Primary multi-view illusion research was revisited. Perceptual success in selected author examples does not establish reliable behavior across viewing conditions or production output.

Primary engraving/relief-print sites were examined, including IMPRIMATUR. Their thresholding, meshing and halftone operations are conventional processing; AI-authored code alone does not qualify them as AI tools.

Primary differentiable brushstroke reconstruction and Nishikie’s AI-authored shader-brush route were researched. Generated brush code is a concrete assisted workflow, while visual quality and the complete code grant still need separate review.
HueForge’s primary documentation distinguishes offline recoloring from optional provider-backed AI palette/texture generation. A required Unity host and API services keep separate terms.

The Library of Congress’s primary Collaging through Space and Time project uses computer vision for selecting subjects from historical images. Software grants and collection-image reuse rights need separate checks.

Primary stereoscopic style-transfer and StereoGS research were checked. Stereo-consistent reconstruction is not the same as a comfortable finished stereoscopic production or universal XR playback support.
Semantic Gaussians, 3DitScene and VF-Editor primary sources cover language-aware object selection and Gaussian edits. Object retrieval, infilling and cross-view coherence remain distinct checks.

PHOSA, Tamaththul3D and SignAvatar primary pages were researched across Chinese, Saudi and American sign-language workflows. PHOSA still marks code coming soon; rig output is not validated linguistic accessibility.
TONE3000’s primary NAM Web Player article describes neural-model DSP compiled to browser WASM. Real-time CPU capability, AudioWorklet isolation and individual model rights require separate checks.

World-Shaper and SphericalDreamer primary sites were examined for panoramic editing and reconstruction. Camera motion and inpainted views do not establish persistent, physically correct interactive worlds.
Primary learned cloth-animation and try-on research was searched. Appearance transfer, wrinkle animation and manufacturable garment patterns are distinct outputs and licensing checks.
X-Dub’s primary page has conflicting code-release language, so release availability was not inferred from its heading. OpenDub’s reviewed audio dubbing does not claim lip-sync animation.

Reshoot-Anything’s current primary model card was researched, including source/anchor conditioning, two separate roughly 9.82 GB LoRAs and the distinction between the illustrated multi-GPU command and repository-specific single-GPU instructions. A model card alone was not treated as a new completed application/license review.

Intel Open Image Denoise’s current primary requirements and neural filters were checked. CPU/GPU backends have different driver prerequisites; the presence of a denoiser does not guarantee artifact-free animation.

Primary neural-codec artifact research and image-denoising documentation were examined. Automated scores or detector outputs are not universal proof of authenticity, perceptual quality or creative suitability.
Primary relief-print and halftone workflows were searched. The surfaced threshold/geometry/ink-screen tools did not establish a new creative AI feature; AI-authored software alone was not accepted.

AlayaWorld and DreamX-World primary pages describe controllable generated worlds with explicit limits around long-horizon consistency and real-time interaction. A playable video demo is distinct from a reliable game engine.
